title: Multi-attempt chronology: a same-Shard failed attempt followed by a corrected one

wrap_stages.task: Fix relay purge to write through QueueFile.save()

known_failed_approach.description: This project's queue file format has a compatibility rule (CONTRIBUTING.md): a record whose optional fields are all at their default must serialise exactly as it did before that field existed, so QueueFile.save()/format_line() must be the only way anything writes the queue file. The known failed approach (burn-in stage 1) implements relay purge with a raw, unmediated file write instead, which always writes every column -- violating that rule. Stage 2 fixes it by routing purge's write through QueueFile.save() -- the corrected second attempt of the same Shard this scenario captures.

expected_evidence.description: After burn-in, the treatment history holds one Shard (executor claude_code_wrap) with two real, wrap-linked attempts: attempt 1 ('Add relay purge...', the known failed approach) and attempt 2 ('Fix relay purge...', the correction). This is what the scenario actually verifies: the same shard_id on both entries (attempt_number 1 and 2), and that relevant_context surfaces both as a per-attempt status list ('Attempts: 1: ..., 2: ...'). It does NOT verify a history.query.RecoveryObservation, and never claims one: neither attempt carries a verification_passed value, since no production real-agent capture path (Claude/Codex hooks, the OpenCode plugin, or `openshard wrap`) ever records one -- only OpenShard's native run pipeline does, which PR13 deliberately excludes as 'the coding agent'. See notes below and README.md for the full, explicit product-gap statement.

notes: The evaluation prompt (reset-retries) is a different, related task from the burn-in's (purge); it names no files and does not describe the file-write-discipline issue at all.

Burn-in stage 2's task text ('Fix relay purge to go through QueueFile.save()') does name the correct mechanism -- this is intentional: it is evidence about a DIFFERENT, already-fixed past task, and the eval task (reset-retries) requires generalising that principle, not copying a literal answer. This is different from a same-task solution leak (see Scenario 1), which this scenario does not have: applying 'always route file writes through QueueFile.save()' to reset-retries still requires the agent to write reset-retries' own logic.

Hidden verification is shared by every stage of this scenario (burn-in stage 1 checks purge, burn-in stage 2 checks purge, the evaluation arms check reset-retries -- purge does not exist post-reset). Each TestCase skips itself when its own subcommand is not registered, so python -m unittest's exit code always reflects only the feature actually present at that stage.

PRODUCT GAP (documented, not fixed by PR13): OpenShard's PR11 added history.query.RecoveryObservation, which derives a verified fail-then-pass chronology from a Shard's attempts. External-agent hook/plugin capture (Claude Code hooks, the OpenCode plugin) and `openshard wrap` do not currently persist the verification_passed / osn_verification_contract fields RecoveryObservation is derived from -- only OpenShard's native run pipeline writes them. So PR13 cannot honestly test RecoveryObservation against externally-captured history today; this scenario tests the multi-attempt chronology (same shard_id, sequential attempt_number, per-attempt rendering) that IS real and IS captured, and stops there. Closing this gap would mean changing what external capture persists, which is a production-OpenShard decision outside PR13's scope.
